info.name: Quicktricks — Courses Access
info.description:
Client-side contracts for course-level listings + PDF access on the secured backend (quicktricks-admin merge, Aug 2026).

**Auth model**
- Listing endpoints are public (pre-login course browsing is a product feature). The **response shape is the security boundary**: listings never contain a fetchable media/PDF URL or raw storage reference.
- The PDF `/access` endpoint takes `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (student login access token).
- Signed URLs are short-lived — request at open time, never persist.

**Migration notes for existing clients**
1. Course class listings no longer include `mp4Recordings`. Media comes exclusively from the class endpoints: `GET /api/classes/:classId/playback` (HLS) and `GET /api/classes/:classId/downloads` (MP4) — see the companion 'Classes Access' collection.
2. A PDF's `isFree` in listings is now the **effective** value: free if EITHER the course placement OR the global PDF flag is free. Render locks off this field directly — it always agrees with what `/access` grants.
3. PDF rows carry an `asset` summary (`state`/`mimeType`/`sizeBytes?`) instead of a URL. To open a PDF, call the `/access` endpoint.

**Variables**: set `baseUrl`, `authToken`, `courseId`, `pdfId`, `userId` at collection level.

variable.description: Test-account email for the Login request / auto-login (use an email-only account — no mobile — to avoid OTP 2FA). Never commit a real value.
Test-account password. Never commit a real value; distribute via a Postman environment.
Set automatically by Login when the account requires OTP 2FA; consumed by Verify login OTP.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Gets a bearer token so every other request works. Set `testEmail` + `testPassword` in the collection variables (or a Postman environment), then either run **Login (get token)** once, or just send any request — the collection pre-request script auto-authenticates whenever `authToken` is missing or expired (expired tokens are **refreshed** via `/api/users/refresh-token` — same session, no new login; missing tokens or failed refreshes fall back to login), and a 401 on any request clears the token so the next send recovers.

Notes:
- If the account has a **mobile number**, the API enforces OTP 2FA: login returns `requiresOtp: true` + a `preAuthToken` (saved automatically), and you must run **Verify login OTP** with the SMS OTP. For hands-off auth use an **email-only** test account.
- The API enforces a **max concurrent session** limit per user (429 with `active_sessions`); the scripts reuse the saved token until it expires or 401s, so normal use stays under the limit.
- Never commit real credentials into the collection file — distribute them via a Postman environment.

exec: console.log('authToken saved — every other request in this collection is now authorized.');

console.warn('This account has a mobile number, so the API requires OTP 2FA. An OTP was sent to ' + json.data.maskedMobile + '. Run "Verify login OTP" next with that OTP. For fully hands-off auth, use an email-only test account (no mobile on the user record).');

request.description: Logs in and saves `data.token` into the `authToken` collection variable (see the Tests tab). Accepts `email` or `mobile` (plus optional `customer_id`). If the account has a mobile number the response is `requiresOtp: true` + `preAuthToken` instead of a token — continue with **Verify login OTP**.

exec: console.error('Refresh failed (' + pm.response.code + '): ' + (json && json.msg) + ' — run Login instead.');

request.description: Single-token refresh: send the CURRENT access token (even if already expired) as the bearer — there is no separate refresh token in this API. The server verifies the signature ignoring expiry, checks the token’s `session_id` is still an active session, and returns a fresh `data.token` (saved into `authToken` automatically). A terminated/logged-out session returns 401 `Session has been terminated` — then a full Login is required. Clients should prefer this over re-login on expiry: it keeps the same session and avoids the max-concurrent-session limit. The collection pre-request script already does this automatically (refresh on expired, login as fallback). Auth is inherited from the collection (`Bearer {{authToken}}`), so just Send.

exec: console.log('authToken saved — every other request in this collection is now authorized.');

request.description: Second step when Login returned `requiresOtp: true` (account has a mobile number). `preAuthToken` was saved automatically by the Login request; paste the 4-digit OTP from SMS. Saves `data.token` into `authToken`.

Public listing of a course's active classes, grouped by topic.

- **`mp4Recordings` is no longer present** on class rows. To play or download a class, use the class endpoints (`/playback`, `/downloads`) with the row's `classId`.
- `isLive` on a class row is a stored scheduling snapshot, not runtime truth — do not gate live UI on it.

- **No `mp4Recordings`** — use the class `/playback` / `/downloads` endpoints for media.

request.description:
Public paginated listing of a course's assigned PDFs.

- `isFree` is the **effective** value (course placement OR global flag) — safe to drive the paid/free lock directly.
- `asset` (`state`/`mimeType`/`sizeBytes?`) replaces any file URL. Open PDFs via the `/access` endpoint below.
- `section`/`topic` names are the placement's own snapshot when present (a shared PDF shows each course's folder names).
- `groupBy=topic` returns `data.topics: [{ topicName, pdfs: [...] }]` instead of the flat paginated shape.

request.description:
Mints a short-lived **signed PDF URL** for a PDF placed in this course. Open/download via `data.url`; re-request rather than persisting.

Access is granted when the placement is free, the PDF is globally free, or the student holds an active order for the course.

**Errors**: `401` unauthenticated · `403` not entitled · `404` course/PDF not found or PDF not placed in this course.

response.name: 403 — not entitled

exec: // Auto-auth: if authToken is missing or expired, obtain one before this request runs.
//   expired + session alive  → POST /api/users/refresh-token (same session, no new login)
//   missing / refresh failed → POST /api/users/login with testEmail/testPassword
// Credentials come from the testEmail + testPassword collection variables (or a
// Postman environment the team distributes — never commit real credentials).
// 30s of slack so a token about to expire is renewed now, not mid-request
// Can't decode — assume it's fine rather than re-authing on every request
// (each login creates a session and the API enforces a max-session limit).
body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ email: email, password: password }) },
console.warn('Auto-login blocked: this account requires OTP 2FA (it has a mobile number). Use the Auth folder manually, or switch testEmail to an email-only account.');
console.warn('Auto-auth: refresh failed (' + (err ? err : res.code + ' ' + (json && json.msg)) + ') — falling back to login.');
// Session-liveness recovery: tokens carry a session_id and die when the session is
// terminated server-side, so expiry checks alone aren't enough. On a 401, clear the
// token — the pre-request auto-login will mint a fresh one on the next send.
console.warn('Got 401 — cleared authToken. Send the request again and auto-login will fetch a fresh token.');
